notes:
**A pixel found on no pages is no longer reported as being on some of them.**

Docket told a site that six advertising pixels were "only on part of the site",
and then listed every one of them as being on **zero** pages. A pixel on zero
pages is not on part of the site, and the finding contradicted its own numbers
in its own sentence.

The cause is that Docket looks for tracking tags twice — in the HTML your server
sends, and again in the page as a browser builds it. Pixels loaded by JavaScript
only show up in the second pass, on the handful of pages Docket renders. They
were being collected from the rendered pages and then counted against the served
HTML, where they never appear.

A pixel Docket can only see after rendering now says so, by name, instead of
being counted as missing from pages nobody looked at properly. A pixel that
really is in your HTML on some pages and not others is still reported, which is
what this check is for — and a gap on a single page now reads "1 page" rather
than "1 pages".
